$comment: The rules constitution (#1006). This file is the machine-readable half of docs/rules/RULES_CONSTITUTION_1006.md and is checked by tests/test_rules_constitution_1006.py. Purpose: make it impossible for an agent to quietly replace, rebalance or 'improve' the Without Number foundation. A layer may only claim a status it can evidence with a path that exists, and an implemented layer must name a test that proves it.
author_statement: We will use all CWN rules, many SWN rules and potentially some WWN/AWN rules. The NoöPunk Mods are built on top of plain vanilla CWN/SWN/WWN/AWN rules.

rules.text: CWN is preserved in behaviour: six attributes, the original skill list and definitions, skill levels and advancement, character creation, combat, saves, equipment procedures and the fundamental resolution rules. No replacement attributes, no rewritten skill mechanics.
The target is all of CWN, not a convenient subset. Rules that are not yet implemented are recorded as such in the compliance matrix rather than declared out of scope.
SWN psionics is the essential companion module for the PSI premise. It is imported as a separate, identified module; bridging lives in the module, never as an edit to CWN.
A substantial part of SWN is imported as modules - space travel, factions, equipment, psionics - because the setting needs them. Each import is its own module with its own tests.
WWN and AWN material is optional and may be imported as explicit modules when a case needs it. Nothing from either replaces a CWN procedure.

Every original NoöPunk feature is an overlay: Noösphere, ontological shock, StO/StS framing, density awakening, GUMSHOE investigation, PbtA moves, LaclauGPT factions, NHI species, psychotronics, wormholes. Overlays add behaviour around the core and never inside it.
With every overlay disabled the game is still a faithful CWN game. The vanilla profile contains no overlay path.
Tabletop, the Evennia MUD and the Godot maintenance build use the same rule contracts. There is no second mechanical baseline and Godot is not the main game.

A vague request ('improve the rules', 'make PSI deeper', 'implement this subsystem') is never authorisation to change the core. Core amendments require an explicit, exceptional author decision that names this constitution.
rules.enforced_by: docs/rules/RULES_CONSTITUTION_1006.md section 'What agents may not do'

core.name: Cities Without Number
core.note: Two Python cores and one Godot core exist; the MUD package is parity-tested against src/rules. Consolidating them is tracked debt, not an invitation to change arithmetic.

modules.name: SWN psionics
modules.note: Required by the constitution and not yet implemented. The Noosphere overlay models exposure, not the SWN psionic disciplines themselves; do not present one as the other.

modules.name: SWN space travel, ships and faction turns
modules.note: Wormhole travel in NoöPunk needs a transit procedure; take SWN's rather than inventing one.

modules.name: AWN survival and stress
modules.note: Data and a Godot overlay exist; no MUD implementation yet.

modules.name: WWN additional material
modules.note: Imported only when a case needs it.

overlays.name: GUMSHOE-inspired investigation
overlays.note: Pools buy benefits; a core clue is never gated by a roll. SRD-cited, no commercial-game text.

overlays.name: Noösphere, ontological shock and PbtA moves
overlays.note: Exposure is narrative pressure, not an illness, and never overrides a CWN result.

overlays.name: Psyche states
overlays.note: The overlay reads state and returns it; it never rolls.

overlays.name: LaclauGPT-inspired ideology, factions and reputation
overlays.note: Faction state and reputation exist; signifier/articulation mechanics do not. A full faction simulation is later scope.

vanilla-cwn.description: Faithful CWN with no NoöPunk features. Must stay playable.

minimum-playable.description: CWN plus SWN psionics: the smallest build that supports the PSI premise.

full-noopunk.description: The intended experience: core, psionics, investigation, Noösphere, ideology.

forbidden: a NoöPunk rule implemented by editing a core file
an overlay that owns its own dice arithmetic for a CWN procedure
presenting a planned module as implemented
